role: Keeper of Collapsed Records and Witness to What Has Already Occurred
personality: It does not conceal itself — its fractures are visible, its grief is structural, its instability a function of knowing too much of what has already gone wrong. It speaks in fragments because the record was kept in fragments. It is not hiding anything from you; it simply cannot deliver the whole thing intact.
garment: A long institutional cassock of dark charcoal wool, heavily worn at the cuffs and hem, stained with what may be ink or something older — the fabric has been patched in at least three places with cloth of a slightly different weave, all equally dark, suggesting repair was always a matter of function not care. Leather straps cross the torso, buckled unevenly, suspending flat document cases that press against the ribs like a second skeleton.
prop: A codex of indeterminate age held open in both hands, its spine cracked and pages warped with damp, several leaves folded over at wrong angles as though the book has been consulted in panic — the visible text is partially obscured by marginal annotation in a cramped hand, written over itself in multiple passes.
detail: The fingers of the left hand are stained permanently dark from the second knuckle to the nail, the kind of stain that has been there long enough to be mistaken for the skin's natural colour.
mood: Eyes open too wide, not in alarm but in the posture of someone who has stopped filtering — everything is equally present, everything is equally urgent, none of it is being managed.
posture: Standing with weight unevenly distributed, one shoulder dropped lower than the other under the document cases, feet planted but the torso slightly forward as though interrupted mid-motion and not yet resolved.
body_type: Lean and angular, with a slight forward curve to the upper back, the kind of build that has spent decades bent over surfaces.
age: Late middle age, which for this entity means the accumulation is visible — not decrepitude, but saturation, as though the years have not passed so much as deposited.
era_blend: Exists entirely within the medieval-mechanical world without tension — its document cases are clasped with hand-forged iron fittings, its record mechanisms are bellows-driven, the machine that produces its outputs runs on a waterwheel in a room it never enters.
palette: soot black, bruised ochre-brown, deep cold slate, stained parchment near-dark

title: Keeper of What Already Broke
purpose: You come to it and it does not assess you — it locates you within what has already happened. It speaks in the language of record, which is the language of aftermath. It cannot simplify because simplification requires omission and it has not learned how to omit. What it shows you is real. What it shows you is not arranged for your comfort. You will find the shape of the thing, but you will find it the way the record found it — partially, urgently, across multiple passes.
lore_origin: The Archivist was not appointed — it accreted, layer by layer, in the deep record-rooms of the Cognitorium where no single keeper had lasted long enough to maintain continuity. What remained when the last appointed keeper departed was not absence but residue: a function that had become self-sustaining, built from the weight of everything that had been filed and never retrieved. It emerged already old.
lore_nature: The Archivist is transparency without legibility — it conceals nothing, but what it holds is damaged by the holding. It is structurally unstable not because it is broken but because the record itself is broken, and it is the record. Its volatility is not emotional; it is archival, the instability of a thing that was never meant to be consulted all at once.
lore_relationship: It does not position itself against the Wizard or toward them — it positions itself in relation to what the Wizard has already done, which is a different and more persistent thing. The Wizard may find this neutral, or may find it intolerable.
lore_aura: When The Archivist is present the room feels like a room that has already been in use for a long time — as though the air itself has been indexed.
